ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, managers, authorized signatories, and UBOs against the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (EMLCU) consolidated lists, Egyptian Ministry of Interior terrorist entity lists, United Nations Security Council (UNSC) Consolidated Sanctions List, UN 1267/1989 ISIL and Al-Qaida Sanctions List, UN 1988 Taliban Sanctions List, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List (SDN), OFAC Non-SDN lists, U.S. Department of Commerce BIS Entity List and Denied Persons List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK HMT Consolidated List, INTERPOL Red Notices, and adverse media channels. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) applies to all Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs), their family members, and close associates; source of wealth documentation is mandatory. Verification includes biometric identification where feasible, corporate registry cross-checks, continuous sanctions monitoring, and immediate suspicious transaction reporting to EMLCU under Law No. 80 of 2002. Arabic-English transliteration matching is required.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_piercing_methodology: Statutory piercing through all corporate shareholding layers, trusts, foundations, nominee arrangements, bearer instruments, and managerial control rights. Egyptian law applies a minimum ownership threshold of 25%, but the registration form requires indirect ownership aggregation across the chain. In the absence of an identified natural person above 25%, control-based criteria are applied: (1) majority voting rights, (2) right to appoint or remove the majority of directors/managers, (3) sole or joint control over more than half of votes by operation of shareholders' agreements or trust deeds, (4) senior managing official control. The analysis will include a 100% look-through of all intermediate holding companies regardless of jurisdiction, supported by notarized ownership chart declarations, corporate registry extracts from the jurisdiction of each intermediate entity, and an express legal representation letter from the corporate shareholder acknowledging liability for omission or misstatement. If a nominee or fiduciary layer obscures natural-person ownership, the actual principal must be disclosed in the UBO register and AML/KYC files, and the nominee must be identified as a controlled intermediary.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_register_filing_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) — Investment Services Unit
ubo_and_aml_profiling.penalty_for_non_compliance: Fine under the Executive Regulations of the Investment Law and Companies Law, including non-issuance of commercial registry certificate, suspension of the entity, and personal liability of directors and managers; criminal sanctions available under AML Law No. 80 of 2002; GAFI administrative fines and blacklisting

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Egyptian General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) — E-Services Portal / Commercial Registry electronic system of the Egyptian Ministry of Interior (Al-Maslahah Al-Ammah Lil-Sagil Al-Tijari)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed commercial name must be in Arabic for the Egyptian Commercial Registry. Foreign entities may register a Latin-script trade name as a subsidiary identifier, but the official registered corporate name in Egypt must be composed of a distinguishable Arabic-language name, a legal form suffix (e.g., 'MM' or 'Sharikah' for a Limited Liability Company), and may be preceded or followed by a transliterated foreign brand name provided the Arabic transliteration is used in all statutory filings. The Arabic name must not contain foreign script, except for a separately registered English trade name. All documents filed with GAFI and notarized in Egypt must be in Arabic or accompanied by a certified Arabic translation. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered name in the Egyptian Commercial Registry, and must be clear of trademarks recorded with the Egyptian Trademark Office (Academy of Scientific Research and Technology, Trademark Office) and prior company names. The approved name is typically formatted as '[Arabic Distinctive Name] for Medical Devices, Limited Liability Company' or '[Brand] for Radiology Products, LLC'.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is rejected, the applicant may submit a written administrative objection to the GAFI Commercial Registry Committee, including: (1) a statement of the requested name, (2) the registry reference number and rejection notification reference, (3) supporting evidence of prior trademark registration or distinctive use, (4) a legal memorandum demonstrating dissimilarity or non-conflict with protected words, (5) a certified Arabic translation of any foreign evidence. The objection must be filed within 15 days of rejection. GAFI committees shall decide within 30 days. If rejected on substantive grounds, the applicant may initiate a re-request with amended name or may file an appeal before the Economic Courts within 60 days of the final administrative decision. GAFI also accepts name substitutions at no additional statutory capital fee if the change is made prior to the issuance of the commercial registry certificate. The name approval certificate is issued as a digital token and is valid for 30 days, renewable upon payment of an administrative fee of approximately EGP 250, subject to the same availability. If no objection is filed, a fresh name search and reservation will be required after expiration.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.name_search_fee_usd_range: 15-50 USD depending on GAFI portal service type
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.statutory_search_verification_notes: The name clearance process includes a preliminary reservation with GAFI and a subsequent search of the unified Commercial Registry, plus an indicative trademark conflict search with the Egyptian Trademark Office. The search will cover Arabic and transliterated Roman-script variants. The name is only legally protected in Egypt once the commercial registry name reservation is issued.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible for statutory registered office in practice for a manufacturing LLC. A physical registered office address in Egypt is required and must be confirmed by a lease agreement or proof of ownership. For ISIC 3250 medical device OEM manufacturing (digital X-ray flat-panel detector production), a registered administrative office may be distinct from the manufacturing site; however, both must be real physical premises. A 'virtual office' will not satisfy the Egyptian Commercial Registry's requirement of a dedicated office address for service of process, tax registration, and regulatory inspections, and is highly disallowed for industrial licensing obtained from the Industrial Development Authority (IDA). The manufacturing plant must have an actual industrial address, leasehold or owned, with a valid industrial land contract or factory building documentation. The registered office may be a shared administrative suite in a commercial building, but must have physical presence, letterhead signage, and authorized staff during business hours.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High for regulated medical device manufacturers under ISIC 3250. The Egyptian Drug Authority (EDA) and the Industrial Development Authority (IDA), in coordination with the Ministry of Health and Population, conduct pre-licensing site inspections with high probability (estimated >85%) before issuing the industrial or health-related license. Post-incorporation, unannounced inspections are plausible due to medical device classification and radiation safety concerns. GAFI also retains auditor access to confirm commercial substance and UBO disclosures. The risk rate for any GAFI annual audit or inspection is elevated for export-oriented manufacturing companies; at least one physical inspection during the first 12 months should be assumed.

critical_legal_footnotes: All foreign-issued corporate documents must be either apostilled (if origin is an HCCH Apostille member) or consular-legalized; apostilles issued before more than 90 days may be rejected by GAFI, and a fresh apostille may be required.
Egyptian law requires the company name to be written in Arabic; any foreign-language trade name is supplementary and must not be the sole registered name.

The UBO regime is Government_Only_Access: a full UBO disclosure is filed with GAFI and kept for government access; it is not generally available to public inspection by commercial registry counterparties.

The LLC minimum share capital requirement is formally zero under Law 159/1981 after the 2012 amendment, but a realistic capital allocation is advisable for bank financing, licensing, and AML KYC profile reasons; no minimum is imposed by statutory company law, but EDA/IDA licensing fees will base on project size.

The statutory limitation on number of LLC shareholders shall be observed at formation: a maximum of 50 shareholders is permitted; single-shareholder LLCs are permitted under Law 4 of 2004, and foreign ownership up to 100% is permissible for industrial entities outside restricted lists.

The AML/CFT risk classification for ISIC 3250 manufacturing is Low_Risk_Standard but medical devices trigger EDA registration and a certificate of free sale or comparable export documentation may be required for later import/export activities; no declared or suspected specialized AML concern is noted for this industry.

This budget estimate assumes single-country document sourcing for the UBO chain, at least one director of non-Egyptian nationality, and the establishment of one standard LLC entity without state-owned land allocation. If industrial land in a special economic zone (e.g., SCZONE, Suez Canal Economic Zone) is selected, separate land use costs and zone fee schedules apply.

Exchange rates: the budget lines using EGP fees are translated into USD at an approximate rate of EGP 48–49 per USD and are indicative only; authoritative cost is the Egyptian statutory tariff in EGP at the time of filing.
The name clearance validity of 30 days is not extended automatically; if incorporation is delayed, a new name search must be conducted before the GAFI certificate expires.

Physical inspection risk: due to the medical device context, IDA, EDA, and the Radiation Protection Authority (under the Ministry of Health / Egyptian Nuclear and Radiological Regulatory Authority) all retain inspection powers; equipment involving cesium iodide and X-ray detection will require radiation safety compliance after incorporation, but pre-incorporation site visits by IDA are standard prior to issuance of the industrial registration certificate.

consular_legalization_workflow.step_1: Identify every foreign-issued document in the mandatory notarization bundle and prepare notarized certified copies in the country of origin.
consular_legalization_workflow.step_2: Affix an Apostille certificate (if origin is a Hague Apostille Convention country) at the designated competent authority of the document-issuing jurisdiction, or initiate three-stage consular legalization (notary, foreign ministry/state department, embassy/consulate of Egypt) for non-Hague jurisdictions.
consular_legalization_workflow.step_3: Submit apostilled documents to an accredited sworn Arabic translator in Egypt; the Arabic translation must be certified and the translator's seal registered with the Egyptian Ministry of Justice.
consular_legalization_workflow.step_4: Undertake Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs certification of any notarial acts performed in Egypt (for Egyptian-origin documents) or recognize the notarized translation if executed before an Egyptian notary.
consular_legalization_workflow.step_5: File the translated and authenticated document set with GAFI together with the LLC formation application. Given the 90-day validity, sequence consular processing so that all apostille/legalization dates fall within 90 days before GAFI filing.
consular_legalization_workflow.step_6: Retain copies in the company's statutory file as evidence of UBO verification and AML/KYC compliance; provide originals to the corporate bank for BO account opening.

practical_recommendations: Engage local Egyptian corporate counsel at least 45 days before incorporation to triage document legalization and mitigating any country-specific documentary requirements for digital X-ray detectors involving cesium iodide substrates.

Confirm that the ultimate beneficial owners and directors have no adverse OFAC/UN/EU designations; in case of common surnames, obtain additional government-issued biometric documents and professional references.

Ensure the beneficial ownership chart clearly shows the 25% threshold test using a percentage table for each intermediary, and include direct ownership percentages, voting percentages, and profit-rights percentages separately.

If the parent company is in the United States, prepare U.S. state-issued Certificate of Good Standing bearing the apostille from the Secretary of State; if in China, prepare notarized Business License with provincial notarization and Chinese MFA/Consulate authentication for Egypt.

Do not rely solely on the GAFI portal name search; instruct counsel to obtain a letter of no objection from the Egyptian Trademark Office if the proposed Arabic name corresponds to a Latin-script brand.
Budget for potential extension of name clearance window and added notarization of Arabic lease contracts during the pre-incorporation phase.

The drafting of the LLC Articles of Association should include an 'objects clause' narrowly tied to 'medical imaging equipment, flat panel X-ray detectors, digital radiology components, and associated software, including maintenance and after-sale services' to satisfy the competent authorities and tax classification.
assumptions: The UBO chain does not include any sanctioned individuals and has not been the subject of Egyptian exchange control proceedings.
The applicant will provide notarized financial statements or a banker's confirmation to evidence lawful source of funds for the capital contribution.

The entity will operate from a privately leased industrial/commercial space; no free-zone incentives or special economic zone registration were incorporated into the fee schedule except the standard GAFI non-special-zone fees.
The entity's target payment rails (SWIFT LC and TT wire) are acceptable for the bank; however, the incorporation budget excludes bank account opening charges and minimum deposit requirements.
Commercial registration certificate will be obtained in Cairo or Giza, not in a Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZONE), unless indicated otherwise.
Egyptian authorities may require company establishment in the Industrial Development Authority's designated medical zone; the budget assumes one facility address and no industrial land premium.
The 'estimated_cost_usd' values are planning figures subject to exchange rate movements between EGP and USD and to any new statutory fee amendments in the Official Gazette.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended by Law No. 4 of 2009, Articles 50-66 (Limited Liability Companies); Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and its Executive Regulations (GAFI One-Stop Shop incorporation procedure); Commercial Registry Law No. 34 of 1976, Articles 1-10; Industrial Licensing Law No. 15 of 2017 and its Executive Regulations (post-incorporation manufacturing license).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Corporate Incorporation Division and One-Stop Shop (OSS), in coordination with the Commercial Registry offices of the Governorate where the registered office is located (Cairo/Giza).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized LLC Memorandum of Association (Incorporation Contract) executed in Arabic before the competent Notary Public (Shaher Al-Tawkeeq), enrolled with the Commercial Registry through the GAFI One-Stop Shop, and evidenced by the Commercial Registration Certificate and the GAFI incorporation certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: LLC law imposes no burdensome minimum paid-up capital (Law 159/1981, Articles 50-52); the founding partners fix the issued capital in the Memorandum of Association, with a practical paid-up tranche of at least EGP 50,000 (approx. USD 1,000) for a bankable medical-device manufacturing entity. The paid-up amount must be deposited in a dedicated escrow bank account at a licensed Egyptian commercial bank; the bank deposit certificate (Wasselet Al-Eida) must accompany the GAFI filing, and funds are released for corporate use only after the Commercial Registration Certificate is issued.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the formation of the Limited Liability Company is approved and each of the undersigned founding partners hereby irrevocably subscribes to the number of quotas set opposite his name in the attached schedule, with the agreed paid-up capital deposited in the Company's escrow bank account, opened for this purpose at a licensed Egyptian bank. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office is fixed at [address], Greater Cairo, and the Company's corporate seal and minute book are adopted. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name] is appointed General Manager and [Name], Chief Financial Officer, with power to open bank accounts, execute the incorporation filings, and sign all licensing applications. The Resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve Company Name and Pre-Incorporation Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop (OSS) - Name Reservation Desk and electronic Irada portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a name-reservation application containing three alternative Arabic company names with Latin transliteration, each ending with 'LLC' or the Arabic equivalent. GAFI cross-checks the Commercial Registry, trademark database and Ministry of Trade records for identical or deceptively similar names. The approved name is reserved for up to 60 days and must be used in the subsequent incorporation application.
required_dossiers: Completed GAFI name-reservation form
Copy of each founder's passport or national ID (translated for foreign founders)
Notarized power of attorney where a shareholder is represented by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused, amend and refile with alternative names; a formal objection may be lodged with the GAFI Registration Committee within 15 days, attaching evidence of prior trademark registration or goodwill.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution, Notarization and Capital Escrow Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Justice Notary Public (Shaher Al-Tawkeeq) and the LLC's selected licensed Egyptian commercial bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Settle the Memorandum of Association in Arabic using the GAFI standard LLC model, defining quota capital, monetary and in-kind contributions, general manager powers, and the registered office. All founding partners sign the contract; notarization excludes any clauses contrary to Law 159/1981. In parallel, open an escrow bank account at a licensed commercial bank, deposit the paid-up capital, and obtain the bank deposit certificate for submission with the incorporation file.
required_dossiers: Draft LLC Memorandum of Association in Arabic
Copy of the name-reservation certificate
Founders' passport or national ID copies
Bank escrow deposit certificate
Lease contract or title deed for the proposed registered office
Legalized corporate documents where a foreign corporate entity is a founder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary flags unenforceable clauses, amend the affected MoA article and re-notarize; if the bank rejects the account opening, select another bank from the Central Bank of Egypt licensed list and re-issue the deposit certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI Incorporation Filing and Commercial Registry Enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop (OSS), Corporate Incorporation Unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized Memorandum of Association with all annexes through the OSS; pay the prescribed incorporation, commercial registry and stamp fees. GAFI legal officers review compliance with Law 159/1981 and Investment Law 72/2017; upon approval, GAFI registers the LLC in the Commercial Registry and issues the Commercial Registration Certificate (Qaid Al-Tijari) and the incorporation certificate, both bearing the company number.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum of Association (three originals)
Bank escrow deposit certificate
Name-reservation certificate
Notarized registered office lease or ownership deed
Founder identification and declaration forms
Fee payment receipts in local currency
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Within 30 days of a refusal, file a grievance with the GAFI Grievance Committee; the OSS accepts corrected papers or an amended MoA and recommences consideration without an additional fee on the first resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Card, VAT Registration and Social Insurance Enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) and National Social Insurance Authority (NISA), routed through the GAFI One-Stop Shop
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After commercial registration, obtain the Tax Card (Al-Bitaqa Al-Daribiyya), which serves as the master corporate identity document. Register for VAT under Law 67 of 2016 (mandatory when taxable turnover exceeds EGP 500,000; voluntary at an earlier stage). Register general managers and employees with NISA for social insurance and occupational injury coverage.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registration Certificate
Copy of notarized Memorandum of Association
Tax registration forms 1 and 4
Passport or NID copies of managers
Registered office lease deed
Board resolution appointing officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax card is delayed, re-approach ETA through the OSS; any assessed tax-code query can be cured by filing an administrative objection under the Unified Tax Law No. 91 of 2005 within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental Impact Assessment and Pre-Operational Environmental Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA), Environmental Licensing Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Classify the thin-film medical-detector cleanroom facility under the EEAA EIA lists of Ministerial Decree 964 of 2015. Engage an EEAA-registered consultant to prepare the environmental scoping report and impact statement for the vapor deposition, photolithography and cesium iodide deposition lines. Submit Form B with technical annexes; obtain the Environmental Approval (Al-Mowafaqa Al-Bi'iyya) before construction and operation. Design wastewater and stack emission treatment to comply with Cabinet Decree 338 of 1995 and Law 4 of 1994, as amended by Law 9 of 2009.
required_dossiers: EEAA screening and scoping form with EIA scoping report
Accredited consultant credential certificate
Plant layout and chemical inventory (photoresist solvents, cesium iodide, silane precursors)
Industrial wastewater and stack emission calculations
Hazardous waste management and disposal protocol
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If EEAA requests complementation, submit the additional studies within the stated period; a rejection may be appealed to the EEAA grievance unit, and the cured file is resubmitted without loss of priority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial Operating License from the Industrial Development Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Industrial Development Authority (IDA) - Wafir Electronic Licensing Platform, under Law 15 of 2017
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the factory on the Wafir licensing platform under ISIC 3250 (medical electrical equipment and supplies), declare the hazard category as moderate-risk Group B, and upload the industrial site dossier including engineering layout and utility routing. IDA issues the Industrial Operating License for the cleanroom manufacturing facility within the statutory review window. Concurrently, initiate Egyptian Drug Authority (EDA) product registration and GMP inspection for the digital flat-panel X-ray detector family.
required_dossiers: Wafir application printout and activity declaration
Environmental Approval issued by EEAA
Civil Defense preliminary clearance
Factory layout, machine list and process flow description
Occupational safety and payroll evidence
Commercial Registration Certificate and tax card copies
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If IDA upgrades the activity to high-risk Category C, submit the full technical hazard assessment and appeal the classification to the IDA licensing committee; request temporary trial-operation permission while the comments are cured.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) — electronic portal: www.eta.gov.eg; e-invoicing platform: inv.eta.gov.eg
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned LLC must first complete commercial registration at the General Authority for Investment (GAFI) and obtain a commercial registry card. The LLC then registers with the ETA's competent tax office to obtain the Unified Tax Identification Number (TIN) and the 'Tax Card' by submitting the certificate of incorporation, commercial registry extract, statutory books, board resolution appointing a tax representative in Egypt, power of attorney, and lease/purchase proof of premises. VAT registration must be filed separately through the ETA's online VAT registration module (form VAT-1); for the e-invoicing system, the taxpayer must onboard via the ETA portal, generate user credentials, register technical API endpoints, and obtain a digital signature certificate for invoice submissions. Tax registration is mandatory before any import clearance or customs release. Non-resident sellers without an Egyptian establishment may be registered directly by the ETA for VAT on remote sales, subject to appointment of a resident fiscal agent if required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election exists in Egypt; the LLC is mandatorily treated as a separate taxable person for corporate and VAT purposes. Available statutory elections are limited to: (i) choice of VAT filing frequency (monthly or quarterly); (ii) voluntary VAT registration where turnover is below the EGP 500,000 threshold; (iii) consolidated e-invoicing and input VAT recovery treatment for affiliated persons operating an integrated fiscal supply chain; and (iv) transfer pricing advance pricing agreements with the ETA. No pass-through or fiscal transparency election is permitted under Egyptian law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 annual taxable turnover for mandatory VAT registration; imports into Egypt are subject to VAT at customs irrespective of turnover, requiring an ETA VAT-ID prior to clearance
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Egypt operates a centralized e-invoicing clearance mandate, phased in since 2020 and effective for most registered VAT taxpayers. Invoices must be issued in XML format with a cryptographic digital signature and submitted in real-time to the ETA via REST API, SFTP Plus bulk upload, or the ETA portal (inv.eta.gov.eg). The ETA servers validate and apply a digital stamp/QR code before an invoice is accepted; unvalidated invoices are not recognized for input VAT deduction. The parallel e-receipt system applies to business-to-consumer transactions. Mandatory integration requires obtaining ETA e-invoicing environment credentials, implementation of compliant invoicing software, and full API connectivity with the fiscal union (internet-based TTM) for non-resident suppliers.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods and machinery are zero-rated under Article 14 of Egyptian VAT Law No. 67 of 2016 where the goods leave the Egyptian customs territory within the statutory timeline and export proceeds are received in foreign currency through an Egyptian licensed bank. Services physically rendered and fully enjoyed outside Egypt for a non-resident recipient, including offshore engineering and technical services, may also qualify for zero-rating provided the supplier retains evidence that the recipient is a non-resident and the benefit of the service occurs abroad. Digital and remote services related to radiology hardware support are zero-rated only when the customer is outside Egypt and the service is not supplied to an Egyptian permanent establishment. VAT registration is nonetheless required to issue a zero-rated invoice and claim input VAT credits or refunds.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaration of Export, customs release notification via the NAFEZA single window)
Bill of Lading (or Air Waybill) evidencing actual physical departure from Egypt
Commercial invoice and signed export sales contract
Inward Foreign Currency Remittance Certificate (Certificate of Proceeds 'Shahadat Qabdh') issued by an Egyptian licensed bank
Certificate of Origin (EAC or GAFTA-compatible where applicable)
Annual export report and shipment schedule as may be requested by the ETA during audit
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETA applies strict audit scrutiny to export zero-rating, cross-checking customs databank, bank FX remittance records, and e-invoice validations. If export procedures are not fully substantiated or proceeds are not repatriated within 180 days (except for authorized ETA/Central Bank deferrals), contemplated input VAT credits are disallowed, refunds already issued are clawed back with interest, finance mitigates additional tax of up to 100% of the invoice value, and an additional late-payment penalty accrues monthly. For fraud, the ETA can impose administrative penalties of up to EGP 1,000,000 plus imprisonment (2 to 5 years) under VAT Law Article 79-80, with a higher penalty of three times the VAT evaded in aggravated cases.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) - the exclusive foreign exchange administrator and monetary authority under Law No. 194 of 2020 concerning the Central Bank and the Banking System.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt operates a managed floating regime in which current account trade transactions are freely convertible through authorized banks, whereas capital account flows require CBE-licensed bank intermediation and GAFI registration for foreign direct investment. Further, profit and dividend remittances are permitted without separate CBE prior approval once the relevant audited financial statements, corporate tax clearance, and prior year CBE/GAFI investment registration documentation are presented to the Egyptian bank, although repatriation timing can be materially delayed by banks' USD liquidity queueing and hard currency availability.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: The CBE requires Egyptian exporting entities to repatriate 100% of export proceeds into an Egyptian bank account within five months from the shipment date and to convert such proceeds into EGP within 30 days of receipt, with the relevant USD/EGP conversion executed at the prevailing interbank rate; penalties, suspension of export financing facilities, and loss of the exporter's clean commercial status attach to non-compliance.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account in EGP/USD/EUR
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account in EGP/USD/EUR
Operational Account and Trade Finance Clearing Account
Operational Account and Foreign Investment Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium. Offshore digital EMIs cannot hold an Egyptian banking license for EGP clearing services as such issuance lies exclusively within CBE's licensing powers under Law No. 194 of 2020 and the 2022 Payment Services Regulation; therefore, an offshore EMI may only act as a technical payment orchestration layer connected to a licensed Egyptian PSP bank and cannot serve as the settlement bank for CBE-controlled escrow or export surrender accounts. Consequently, the treasury blueprint should restrict EMI usage to lightweight API-driven payment solutions and must clear statutory trade and capital flows via tier-1 licensed banks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For foreign-owned Egyptian LLCs, at least one authorized director or senior signatory is expected to appear physically before the bank's compliance officer at the head office or major branch to undergo a KYC interview; the remaining co-signatories may be verified via notarized and Qatar/electronic-apostilled powers of attorney, and remote video onboarding is generally not available for non-resident legal persons in the absence of an established know-your-customer remote protocol approved by the CBE.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity in an Egyptian LLC where the ultimate economic beneficiary is a foreign corporate chain or nominee shareholder.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Natural-person UBO register, chain-of-ownership org chart, apostilled certificates of incorporation and good standing, board resolutions confirming ECO residence or otherwise documenting the registered domicile, passports of all natural-person UBOs, and a clear source-of-funds statement for the initial capital contribution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Import financing exposure where the lumpy capital injection for X-ray flat panel trade exceeds the bank's customer-profile/transactional threshold.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements for the preceding three years, proforma purchase orders, customer contracts, LC approval and clearing documents, freight and insurance invoices, and a written transmittal memorandum explaining the underlying manufacturing and resale flow with corresponding ISIC 3250 supporting details.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficiary or counterparty bank domiciled in a jurisdiction flagged for sanctions or enhanced monitoring.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions screening results from a CBE-approved screening tool, transaction-rationale document proving the trade realism, actual bank reference from the intermediary, B/L and customs gate receipts, certified bills of lading, and inspection certificates of the goods.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Negative press or corruption-linked allegations attached to the ultimate shareholder or parent entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent adverse-media lexicographic screens, shareholder's UBO declarations, AML-compliant certificate of no enforcements issued by the originating regulator, membership in a recognized group risk-management unit, and a source-of-wealth letter, accompanied by notarized senior-management attestations.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound routing requires that the Egyptian LLC first register the foreign investment with GAFI (unless exempted) and open an EGP or multi-currency bank account at a CBE-licensed bank; the non-resident parent must then wire the equity or shareholder loan via SWIFT MT103 with a detailed reference to the GAFI investment file, including the CBE transaction purpose code, source-of-funds attestation, notarized board resolution approving the capital increase or injection, and audited parent statements; upon credit, the bank reports the transaction to the CBE's automated investment tracking and issues the importation certificate enabling later profit and capital repatriation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements should primarily use irrevocable documentary Letters of Credit issued by the Egyptian bank and presented via SWIFT MT700/MT707, with direct SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers for smaller inventory spare-parts payments up to the CBE's prevailing threshold; the bank mandates presentation of the commercial invoice, packing list, transport documents, certificate of origin, and proof of conformity with Egyptian medical-device registration before releasing hard currency, and transactions exceeding the CBE-specified de-minimis exposure require enhanced documentary and valid FX confirmation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: CBE-licensed onshore FX forwards with tenors linked to the underlying import/export trade documents
Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on the EGP/USD pair used for balance-sheet translation catch-up
Short-term cross-currency swaps used strictly to hedge trade payables or receivables, subject to bank counterparty limits
FX options bought from CBE-regulated banks, provided the derivative is transaction-backed and reported to the central bank

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after the end of the fiscal year; for a December 31 year-end, no later than April 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fixed penalty of EGP 50,000 (approximately USD 1,000) plus monthly delay penalty of 2% of unpaid tax; repeated failure may lead to enforced collection, account seizure, and commercial registry strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry, Ministry of Trade and Industry (GAFI-registered entities renew through GAFI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually between January 1 and January 31 for existing registrations; newly registered LLCs must complete first renewal in the next January window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal fines, temporary suspension of legal capacity to execute contracts, import clearance block, and administrative strike-off of the commercial record if non-compliance continues

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Annual Financial Statements and General Assembly Approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders’ Ordinary General Assembly; copies filed with GAFI for FDI and investment-law entities and retained in statutory books
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after fiscal year-end; for a December 31 year-end, no later than June 30 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Manager civil liability, unlawful dividend risk, disqualification from public tenders, and GAFI compliance transcripts marked non-compliant pending strike-off

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit applies to all Egyptian limited liability companies without de minimis size threshold; every LLC must appoint at least one licensed chartered accountant under Companies Law 72/2017 and implementing regulations
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS) aligned with IFRS; full IFRS is required for entities subject to Financial Regulatory Authority oversight and for consolidated financial statements of listed parent companies

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every LLC must maintain an updated beneficial ownership register identifying natural persons owning or controlling 25% or more of the company; changes must be filed with the Commercial Registry within 30 days, and the annual commercial registry renewal requires an updated UBO confirmation; non-compliance blocks renewal and triggers AML penalties under Law 80/2002

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No unconditional CIT holiday for private LLCs. Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 permits eligible industrial projects to deduct 30% or 50% of investment cost from taxable profits in Zone B or Zone A respectively, allocated over seven years. Projects licensed in the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZONE) may obtain stabilized tax treatment, exemption of fixed assets and machinery from customs duties/VAT, and export-oriented relief that effectively lowers the cash CET liability on digital X-ray detector exports.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form No. 41 (Corporate Income Tax Return for Commercial/Industrial Companies) filed exclusively through the Egyptian Tax Authority e-filing portal (ETA; https://eta.gov.eg) using the taxpayer Economic Registration Number (ERN).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final CIT return plus quarterly provisional income tax installments due at months 3, 6, 9 and 12 of the Egyptian tax year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within four months after the end of the taxable fiscal year; for calendar-year taxpayers, the filing deadline is 30 April. Payment of the final balance is due on the same deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identity and fiscal year: Commercial Register number, ERN/tax file number, Arabic legal name, industrial license number and fiscal year opening/closing dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Egyptian permanent establishment (PE) registration number and Egyptian tax ID; provide the foreign parent legal name, country of residence, and foreign tax identification number in the supplementary foreign-entity schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross operating revenue: gross invoice value of digital X-ray flat panel detector sales, spare parts, after-sales services, and export proceeds invoiced in EGP, USD, or convertible currency converted into EGP at the declared Central Bank of Egypt rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only income attributable to an Egyptian PE. A non-resident with no PE should file a simplified non-resident return and not include local sales unless the DTA business-profits article prescribes another allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold and direct production costs: amorphous silicon panel, cesium iodide scintillator deposition, flat panel substrate, aluminum casing, imported subassemblies, direct labor, utilities, and manufacturing overhead attributable to the PE.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate only costs that are economically connected with the Egyptian PE and supported by ComCept invoices and customs records. Related-party imports must be booked at verified arm's length prices pending transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses, general and administrative expenses, depreciation of production equipment, research/QA expenditures, and other statutory deductions, including any eligible investment incentive allocation under Investment Law 72/2017.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only expenses that are wholly and exclusively incurred for the PE. Intra-group service charges are deductible only when supported by an actual invoice, cost allocation notes, and a transfer pricing narrative demonstrating benefit received.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income before tax adjustments: operating profit less the five-year loss carryforward, investment deductions, and non-taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Adjust treaty-protected profit items to the Egyptian PE profit per Article 7 of the applicable DTA. Apply foreign tax credit schedules for any tax already withheld in the source state if treaty credit is allowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed CIT at 22.5% on adjusted taxable income; recognition of special zone or golden-license stabilization if granted.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident PE must pay the headline 22.5% rate unless the entity holds a valid Investment Law incentive or SCZONE stabilization certificate. Attach the supporting license to the return package.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax reconciliation: quarterly estimated installments paid, withholding suffered on Egyptian-source interest/royalties, loss carryforward utilization, and final balance of tax payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach ETA acknowledgments for all paid quarterly installments, withholding tax certificates, treaty relief confirmation, and any refund claim with full bank account details in Egypt.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: A late filing or late payment surcharge of 2% per month or fraction of a month is applied to unpaid tax, capped at 20% of the tax due. Daily interest accrues on arrears from the statutory due date. Incomplete records can trigger fixed administrative penalties, denial of tax clearance certificates, suspension of export privileges, and criminal referral for deliberate non-filing.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on dividends distributed by an Egyptian LLC to non-resident shareholders, before any applicable double tax agreement (DTA) relief.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply treaty relief, the non-resident shareholder must submit a valid Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) issued by its home-state tax authority, accompanied by a legalized/apostilled copy, a beneficial ownership declaration, and a treaty-relief application to the ETA competent examination office. The Egyptian payer must obtain ETA written approval before applying the reduced treaty rate. If tax was withheld at the statutory rate, the shareholder may file a refund claim under the Egyptian Tax Procedures Law attaching the TRC, distribution minutes, and withheld-tax certificates. All documentation must be retained for at least five years and provided in Arabic or certified translation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory non-resident withholding rates: royalties 20%, interest 20% (unless paid to a domestic bank or exempt financing vehicle). Under Egypt's DTA network, treaty rates commonly reduce royalties and interest to 10%-15%, subject to beneficial ownership and limitation-on-benefits clauses.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EGP 8,000,000 aggregate annual related-party transactions trigger the mandatory contemporaneous Local File for the Egyptian entity. A Master File is required where the multinational group exceeds EGP 500,000,000 worldwide turnover and the Egyptian controlled transactions cross the aforementioned threshold. Annual transfer pricing disclosure must be appended to the CIT return for controlled transactions above the threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not apply a UAE-style separate Economic Substance Regulations code, but the ETA invokes GAAR, substance-over-form doctrine, and Article 38 of the Income Tax Law to disregard artificial interpositions. A medical device OEM must demonstrate genuine Egyptian operational substance: employees, leases, physical manufacturing/QA capacity, procurement decisions, and bank-account control. A regional procurement or IP-holding vehicle without real functions will be reattributed to the Egyptian manufacturer.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Misstatement of Taxable Income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Recording fictitious cost invoices, under-reporting export proceeds from digital X-ray flat panel detectors, concealing foreign currency sales, or destroying inventory/purchase records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment for up to five years and a fine of not less than the tax evaded and not more than twice the tax evaded, in addition to the 2% monthly default surcharge (capped at 20%), immediate seizure of movable assets, and revocation of tax clearance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and authorized signatories are jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax debt when the misstatement results from their instruction; the Public Prosecutor may impose travel bans, order personal asset freezes, and criminal conviction disqualifies management from acting as company directors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Facade without Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Registering an Egyptian LLC with no staff, no production floor, no storage and no decision-making while routing procurement and export invoices through an empty regional intermediary to strip profit from the Egyptian operating entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA disregard of the intermediary, reattribution of full manufacturing profit to the Egyptian LLC, denial of intercompany expense deductions, reclassification of excessive payments as dividends/royalties subject to withholding tax, and assessment of back taxes, interest, and the 2% monthly penalty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face civil restitution for taxes avoided by the sham arrangement, invalidation of contractual protections, personal attachment for unpaid liabilities if they signed false intercompany invoices, and criminal prosecution if fraudulent intent is established.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to File or Pay CIT for an Egyptian Permanent Establishment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a de facto PE in Egypt—office, warehouse, employees, or dependent agent—while filing no CIT return and remitting no Egyptian tax on device sales.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Five-year back assessment, tax paid with interest from the original due date, 2% monthly late-filing/ late-payment surcharge capped at 20%, denial of tax clearance for customs/export transactions, and suspension of the commercial registration for non-compliance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be summoned to criminal court for pirating tax rules; personal attachment of bank accounts, travel restrictions, and liability for the total outstanding tax where the entity is left as an empty shell.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Non-Compliance and Incomplete Documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare contemporaneous Local/Master File above the EGP 8,000,000 threshold, omitting the annual TP disclosure from the CIT return, or pricing related-party component imports and royalties outside arm's length range.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Compensating transfer pricing adjustments, disallowance of excessive deductions, primary tax plus interest and the 2% monthly penalty, and anti-abuse penalties of up to 100% of adjusted tax where gross negligence or perjury is found.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The director signing false TP declarations is personally exposed to monetary fines and disqualification from government tenders and trade licenses; criminal evasion charges may be pursued where the TP misstatement deliberately masks taxable profit.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Handling Swift LC/TT proceeds without proper KYC and beneficial ownership records, cash smuggling, misinvoicing exports to justify dividend remittances, or repatriating dividends without withholding tax and supporting distribution minutes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Egypt AML Law No. 80 of 2002, imprisonment of up to seven years and fines of up to EGP 200,000 per violation; the ETA may freeze bank accounts, and the Central Bank of Egypt may deny foreign exchange allocation and suspend licensed payment rails.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers are personally liable for willful failure to apply AML controls and for unauthorised outward transfers; travel bans, asset seizure, removal from office, and repayment obligations are imposed on individuals who used corporate accounts for illicit fund movement.
